actions.text: Received in the Senate and Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
Motion to reconsider laid on the table Agreed to without objection.
On motion to suspend the rules and pass the bill Agreed to by the Yeas and Nays: (2/3 required): 336 - 36 (Roll no. 192). (text: CR H3212-3213)
Passed/agreed to in House: On motion to suspend the rules and pass the bill Agreed to by the Yeas and Nays: (2/3 required): 336 - 36 (Roll no. 192).
Considered as unfinished business. (consideration: CR H3231)

At the conclusion of debate, the Yeas and Nays were demanded and ordered. Pursuant to the provisions of clause 8, rule XX, the Chair announced that further proceedings on the motion would be postponed.
DEBATE - The House proceeded with forty minutes of debate on H.R. 1770.
Considered under suspension of the rules. (consideration: CR H3212-3214)
Mr. Latta moved to suspend the rules and pass the bill.
Placed on the Union Calendar, Calendar No. 123.
Reported by the Committee on Energy and Commerce. H. Rept. 119-157.

dimensions.assessment: Affects federal regulatory agencies (CPSC, FTC, Department of Commerce), technologists, product manufacturers, and consumers.
dimensions.evidence: consult with relevant stakeholders, such as data scientists and product manufacturers, and use artificial intelligence

dimensions.assessment: Primarily requires pilot programs, studies, reports, and stakeholder consultations rather than enforcing major regulatory overhauls.
Involves administrative costs for conducting pilot programs and producing federal reports without specifying new major appropriations.
Directs specific federal agencies to execute pilot testing, research studies, and congressional reporting.
dimensions.evidence: the Consumer Product Safety Commission shall establish a pilot program to explore the use of artificial intelligence

dimensions.assessment: Primarily governs short-term pilot programs, studies, and reporting requirements concluding within fixed timeframes.

missing_information: Specific funding amounts allocated for the CPSC artificial intelligence pilot program are not mentioned.
importance_detail.rationale: The bill requires the Consumer Product Safety Commission to establish an artificial intelligence pilot program for product safety and directs the Department of Commerce and Federal Trade Commission to conduct studies and submit reports on blockchain technology and digital tokens.
